Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\explorer.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\RuntimeBroker.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard Installation High
ConnectWise / AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installed outside IT change windows = common tradecraft for ransomware affiliates and IT-helpdesk impersonators.
ATT&CKT1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe")
   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)kaseya.*\.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\atera_agent.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\SplashtopStreamer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\RustDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\NinjaOne.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

status: experimental
description: |

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("77.110.122.58", "213.165.41.26") or RemoteUrl has_any ("cl.distritovagas.com", "sonra.eutialyson.com", "anus-staylard.xyz", "resumeacceptable.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["77.110.122.58", "213.165.41.26"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["cl.distritovagas.com", "sonra.eutialyson.com", "anus-staylard.xyz", "resumeacceptable.com"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("2abe5dd3a057fdef935722e50e9251c272d29fd26113187b853a1f9a9cb89d9b", "3b7ae925e2d64522b4f69b56285b05aeca8c5aab5ab46a9c02c4fafb69d881ce", "cd4e5e2c65b1660470d3446539ee68adf5faeece3eaeb46583623be9911ee145", "79f7b67ce8b39070f3e1c2b90fce0ce84134782a7dedcccc1edac197ee9e089b", "2ada24dd6e517f37942b749c2bd57ddd97445e9853002cee70a0bc30d0b0ce3a") or SHA1 in~ ("2abe5dd3a057fdef935722e50e9251c272d29fd26113187b853a1f9a9cb89d9b", "3b7ae925e2d64522b4f69b56285b05aeca8c5aab5ab46a9c02c4fafb69d881ce", "cd4e5e2c65b1660470d3446539ee68adf5faeece3eaeb46583623be9911ee145", "79f7b67ce8b39070f3e1c2b90fce0ce84134782a7dedcccc1edac197ee9e089b", "2ada24dd6e517f37942b749c2bd57ddd97445e9853002cee70a0bc30d0b0ce3a") or MD5 in~ ("2abe5dd3a057fdef935722e50e9251c272d29fd26113187b853a1f9a9cb89d9b", "3b7ae925e2d64522b4f69b56285b05aeca8c5aab5ab46a9c02c4fafb69d881ce", "cd4e5e2c65b1660470d3446539ee68adf5faeece3eaeb46583623be9911ee145", "79f7b67ce8b39070f3e1c2b90fce0ce84134782a7dedcccc1edac197ee9e089b", "2ada24dd6e517f37942b749c2bd57ddd97445e9853002cee70a0bc30d0b0ce3a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("2abe5dd3a057fdef935722e50e9251c272d29fd26113187b853a1f9a9cb89d9b", "3b7ae925e2d64522b4f69b56285b05aeca8c5aab5ab46a9c02c4fafb69d881ce", "cd4e5e2c65b1660470d3446539ee68adf5faeece3eaeb46583623be9911ee145", "79f7b67ce8b39070f3e1c2b90fce0ce84134782a7dedcccc1edac197ee9e089b", "2ada24dd6e517f37942b749c2bd57ddd97445e9853002cee70a0bc30d0b0ce3a") or SHA1 in~ ("2abe5dd3a057fdef935722e50e9251c272d29fd26113187b853a1f9a9cb89d9b", "3b7ae925e2d64522b4f69b56285b05aeca8c5aab5ab46a9c02c4fafb69d881ce", "cd4e5e2c65b1660470d3446539ee68adf5faeece3eaeb46583623be9911ee145", "79f7b67ce8b39070f3e1c2b90fce0ce84134782a7dedcccc1edac197ee9e089b", "2ada24dd6e517f37942b749c2bd57ddd97445e9853002cee70a0bc30d0b0ce3a") or MD5 in~ ("2abe5dd3a057fdef935722e50e9251c272d29fd26113187b853a1f9a9cb89d9b", "3b7ae925e2d64522b4f69b56285b05aeca8c5aab5ab46a9c02c4fafb69d881ce", "cd4e5e2c65b1660470d3446539ee68adf5faeece3eaeb46583623be9911ee145", "79f7b67ce8b39070f3e1c2b90fce0ce84134782a7dedcccc1edac197ee9e089b", "2ada24dd6e517f37942b749c2bd57ddd97445e9853002cee70a0bc30d0b0ce3a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["2abe5dd3a057fdef935722e50e9251c272d29fd26113187b853a1f9a9cb89d9b", "3b7ae925e2d64522b4f69b56285b05aeca8c5aab5ab46a9c02c4fafb69d881ce", "cd4e5e2c65b1660470d3446539ee68adf5faeece3eaeb46583623be9911ee145", "79f7b67ce8b39070f3e1c2b90fce0ce84134782a7dedcccc1edac197ee9e089b", "2ada24dd6e517f37942b749c2bd57ddd97445e9853002cee70a0bc30d0b0ce3a"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).

title: Crypto-Wallet Keystore Access by Non-Wallet Process
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d02
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers / wallet drainers read keystore files from MetaMask,
    Exodus, Atomic, Phantom, Bitcoin, Electrum, Ethereum-cli wallets.
    Filtering out the legitimate wallet binaries leaves only attacker
    activity.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1005/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1005
    - attack.collection
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Ethereum\keystore\'
            - '\Bitcoin\'
            - '\Exodus\'
            - '\Electrum\wallets\'
            - '\MetaMask\'
            - '\Phantom\'
            - '\Atomic\Local Storage\'
    filter_legit:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\MetaMask.exe'
            - '\Exodus.exe'
            - '\Atomic.exe'
            - '\electrum.exe'
            - '\Bitcoin.exe'
            - '\Phantom.exe'
    condition: selection_path and not filter_legit
falsepositives:
    - Backup software
level: high

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high

Junior Hacker Used Tailscale and OpenSSH to Keep Access After His C2 Went Offline

The Hacker News
2026-06-17 18 use cases 5 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

A French-speaking attacker broke into a small French automotive business, planted a keylogger, and stole banking and email credentials. Ordinary stuff, until one move near the end. Before his command-and-control server went dark, he installed OpenSSH and Tailscale on a victim's machine, building a way back in that did not run through the C2 at all. When the Havoc server went offline the next

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] certutil smart-card / certificate store enumeration
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] wscript/cscript executing .vbs from user staging folder (Poisson VBScript stager)
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Junior Hacker Used Tailscale and OpenSSH to Keep Access After His C2 Went Offlin
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] OpenSSH Server install on Windows workstation (Poisson persistence pivot) · [LLM] Logon-trigger scheduled task at HIGHEST privileges launching script interpreter · [LLM] authorized_keys file write on Windows host (SSH key persistence) · Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Tailscale client install or tailnet connection (100.100.100.0/8 / login.tailscale.com) · [LLM] SSH reverse tunnel (ssh -R) outbound from Windows endpoint · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] powercfg disabling standby/hibernate to keep host harvest-ready · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change
OpenSSH Server install on Windows workstation (Poisson persistence pivot) AIInstallation High
Detects Add-WindowsCapability adding the OpenSSH.Server feature, sshd.exe service start, or registry/firewall configuration enabling sshd on a Windows endpoint. Article-specific: Poisson installed OpenSSH on April 7 as a C2-independent reentry path so access survived the Havoc takedown. Rationale: Cato's first hunt-list item is literally 'OpenSSH Server installs on a Windows workstation, which is rarely legitimate.' Defender ships OpenSSH as a FoD capability — Add-WindowsCapability/dism/sshd.exe are the three install vectors; combining them with non-machine accounts keeps this near-zero FP.
ATT&CKT1133 T1021.004 T1505
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Dev/SRE workstation where the user genuinely needs sshd to test Ansible/Terraform from WSL
  • IT pilot enabling RemoteSSH for management at scale
  • Visual Studio Code 'Remote-SSH' setup wizard installing the OpenSSH client (not server)
  • Lab/test image being provisioned by Packer
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("MsiExec.exe","TrustedInstaller.exe") and AccountName !in~ ("SYSTEM","LOCAL SERVICE","NETWORK SERVICE")
Response runbook
Triage: pivot on the host's last 24h DeviceProcessEvents — look for VBS->PowerShell->.NET chain (Havoc Demon staging), Tailscale process, RustDesk install, schtasks /Create at logon, and any keylogger artifact under user staging dirs. Check DeviceLogonEvents for new inbound RemoteInteractive logons after install. Contain: stop the sshd service, disable the OpenSSH.Server capability, remove host firewall allow rule for TCP/22, block egress to login.tailscale.com and DuckDNS at edge, isolate the host. Hunt: across the org, query for tailscale.exe execution, ssh.exe with -R flag, schtasks /RL HIGHEST /SC ONLOGON launching script interpreters, and powercfg standby-timeout-* 0 over the same 30d window.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Add-WindowsCapability","OpenSSH.Server","Start-Service sshd","Set-Service -Name sshd"))
   or (FileName =~ "dism.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "OpenSSH")
   or FileName =~ "sshd.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where AccountType =~ "User"
| where (NewProcessName endswith @"\powershell.exe" and CommandLine has_any ("Add-WindowsCapability","OpenSSH.Server","Start-Service sshd"))
   or (NewProcessName endswith @"\dism.exe" and CommandLine has "OpenSSH")
   or NewProcessName endswith @"\sshd.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: OpenSSH Server Capability Install on Windows Workstation
id: a7d2e9c4-3f8b-4f1a-9b6e-2c5d8e7f1a4b
description: Detects installation/start of OpenSSH Server feature on a Windows endpoint, as used by 'Poisson' for a C2-independent reentry path.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/junior-hacker-used-tailscale-and.html
author: thn-usecases
date: 2026/06/17
tags:
  - attack.t1133
  - attack.t1021.004
  - attack.t1505
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_addcap:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\dism.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'Add-WindowsCapability'
      - 'OpenSSH.Server'
      - 'Start-Service sshd'
      - 'Set-Service -Name sshd'
  selection_sshd:
    Image|endswith: '\sshd.exe'
  condition: 1 of selection_*
level: high
source:(windows.security OR windows.sysmon) ((@Image:(*\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\dism.exe OR *\DISM.EXE) AND @CommandLine:(*Add-WindowsCapability* OR *OpenSSH.Server* OR *"Start-Service sshd"*)) OR @Image:(*\sshd.exe OR *\SSHD.EXE))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 (ImageFileName=/\\sshd\.exe$/i OR (ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh|dism)\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/(Add-WindowsCapability|OpenSSH\.Server|Start-Service\s+sshd)/i)) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name=powershell.exe OR Processes.process_name=pwsh.exe) AND (Processes.process="*Add-WindowsCapability*OpenSSH.Server*" OR Processes.process="*Set-Service*sshd*Automatic*" OR Processes.process="*Start-Service*sshd*") OR Processes.process_name=sshd.exe OR (Processes.process_name=dism.exe AND Processes.process="*OpenSSH*") by host Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where user!="*$" | sort - firstTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name=powershell.exe OR Processes.process_name=pwsh.exe) AND (Processes.process="*Add-WindowsCapability*OpenSSH.Server*" OR Processes.process="*Set-Service*sshd*Automatic*" OR Processes.process="*Start-Service*sshd*") OR Processes.process_name=sshd.exe OR (Processes.process_name=dism.exe AND Processes.process="*OpenSSH*") by host Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where user!="*$" | sort - firstTime
Tailscale client install or tailnet connection (100.100.100.0/8 / login.tailscale.com) AICommand & Control High
Surfaces tailscale.exe/tailscaled.exe execution, tailscale-up commands, DNS for login.tailscale.com, or any traffic into the 100.64.0.0/10 CGNAT / 100.100.100.0/24 magic-DNS range. Article-specific: Poisson joined victim machines to his private tailnet for a fully out-of-band reentry path that survived the Havoc takedown. Rationale: Cato names Tailscale outright as Poisson's 'separate door' and the article gives the magic-DNS IP 100.100.100.2 and login.tailscale.com as pivot indicators. The detection joins process telemetry (tailscale.exe/up/login) and network telemetry (100.100.100/24, port 41641, control-plane DNS) so it catches the install AND the active tunnel.
ATT&CKT1572 T1219 T1090
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Engineering team using Tailscale as their official corporate VPN
  • Remote SRE accessing infra over a documented tailnet
  • Personal Tailscale install on a BYOD/AAD-registered laptop that's also on the corp tenant
  • Tailscale being silently bundled by another tool like Headscale or NextDNS
Suppression filter
| where DeviceName !in (dynamic(["<approved-tailscale-hosts>"])) and InitiatingProcessAccountName !in~ ("SYSTEM","<corp-IT-deployment-account>")
Response runbook
Triage: confirm whether the host is in IT's Tailscale-approved inventory; if not, pull DeviceProcessEvents 24h before/after the install for a Havoc/RustDesk staging chain and check DeviceLogonEvents for inbound RemoteInteractive over 100.x.x.x. Contain: kill tailscaled, uninstall the package, block login.tailscale.com + controlplane.tailscale.com + derp*.tailscale.com at proxy, deny 100.64.0.0/10 egress at edge, revoke the tailnet auth key if obtainable. Hunt: pivot org-wide for any host that resolved login.tailscale.com over the past 90d but is not on the approved list; correlate with OpenSSH installs and powercfg standby changes on the same host.
let TS_Proc = DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("tailscale.exe","tailscaled.exe")
   or (ProcessCommandLine has_any (" up --authkey"," up --login-server","tailscale login","tailscale up") and ProcessCommandLine has "tailscale")
   or FolderPath has @"\Tailscale\"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName;
let TS_Net = DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("login.tailscale.com","controlplane.tailscale.com","derp.tailscale.com")
   or RemoteIP startswith "100.100.100."
   or (RemotePort == 41641 and RemoteIPType == "Public")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
union isfuzzy=true TS_Proc, TS_Net
| order by Timestamp desc
let TS_Proc = SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\tailscale.exe" or NewProcessName endswith @"\tailscaled.exe" or CommandLine has_any ("tailscale up","tailscale login","--authkey")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName;
let TS_Net = DnsEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Name has_any ("login.tailscale.com","controlplane.tailscale.com","derp")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name;
union isfuzzy=true TS_Proc, TS_Net
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Tailscale Client Activation on Endpoint
id: b8e3facd-4f9c-4f2b-ac7f-3d6e9f8a2b5c
description: Detects tailscale.exe/tailscaled.exe execution or tailnet bootstrap commands on a Windows endpoint, per Cato CTRL's hunt for 'Poisson's' Tailscale fallback channel.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/junior-hacker-used-tailscale-and.html
author: thn-usecases

  selection_cmd:

      - 'tailscale up'

      - '--authkey'

source:(windows.security OR windows.sysmon) (@Image:(*\tailscale.exe OR *\Tailscale.exe OR *\TAILSCALE.EXE OR *\tailscaled.exe OR *\Tailscaled.exe) OR @CommandLine:(*"tailscale up"* OR *"tailscale login"* OR *--authkey* OR *--login-server*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 (ImageFileName=/\\tailscale(d)?\.exe$/i OR CommandLine=/(tailscale\s+(up|login)|--authkey|--login-server)/i) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
NETWORK

| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name=tailscale.exe OR Processes.process_name=tailscaled.exe OR Processes.process="*tailscale*up*" OR Processes.process="*tailscale*login*") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | append [| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest_ip=100.64.0.0/10 OR All_Traffic.dest="login.tailscale.com" OR All_Traffic.dest="controlplane.tailscale.com" OR All_Traffic.dest_port=41641 by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_ip All_Traffic.dest_port All_Traffic.app | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`] | sort - count

SSH reverse tunnel (ssh -R) outbound from Windows endpoint AICommand & Control High
Detects ssh.exe invoked with `-R <port>` (remote-port-forward) to an external host — the technique Poisson used to expose victim ports back through his SSH listener. Tier alerting because ssh.exe with -R on a workstation is overwhelmingly attacker tradecraft. Rationale: Cato's hunt list calls out 'ssh -R reverse tunnels heading to outside hosts' verbatim. The regex `-R <bind>:<port>` keys on Poisson's actual SSH-listener setup; pairing with `AccountName !endswith "$"` and `ssh.exe` on a workstation (vs. server) keeps the FP cone tight.
ATT&CKT1572 T1021.004 T1571
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer using ngrok-style SSH reverse tunnel to expose a local dev server
  • DevOps engineer port-forwarding through a bastion for debugging
  • GitHub Actions self-hosted runner setup script
  • Educational SSH tutorial run by a curious user
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("code.exe","WindowsTerminal.exe","git-bash.exe") and DeviceName !startswith "DEV-"
Response runbook
Triage: extract the destination from `ReverseSpec` — passive-DNS / WHOIS / abuse.ch checks on the bind host; pull DeviceNetworkEvents from that host for the same time window. Contain: kill the ssh.exe process tree, block the destination IP at egress, rotate any private keys cached in %USERPROFILE%\.ssh\ on the host. Hunt: cross-org search for ssh.exe -R, OpenSSH server installs, and Tailscale activations on the same host within 30 days — Poisson chained all three.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName =~ "ssh.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(^|\s)-R\s+(\S*:)?\d{1,5}(:[^\s]+:\d{1,5})?"
| extend ReverseSpec = extract(@"(?i)(?:^|\s)-R\s+(\S+)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, ReverseSpec, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where AccountType =~ "User"
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\ssh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(^|\s)-R\s+(\S*:)?\d{1,5}"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: SSH Reverse Tunnel Outbound from Windows Endpoint

description: ssh.exe spawned with -R (remote port forward) on a Windows host — Poisson's outbound reverse-tunnel pattern in the Cato CTRL writeup.
references:

  condition: selection
level: high
source:(windows.security OR windows.sysmon) @Image:(*\ssh.exe OR *\SSH.EXE OR *\Ssh.exe) @CommandLine:(*" -R "* OR *" -R3"* OR *" -R 1"* OR *" -R 2"* OR *" -R 4"* OR *" -R 5"* OR *" -R 6"* OR *" -R 7"* OR *" -R 8"* OR *" -R 9"*)

wscript/cscript executing .vbs from user staging folder (Poisson VBScript stager) AIDelivery High
Detects wscript.exe or cscript.exe running a .vbs script out of Downloads, Temp, AppData, Public, or ProgramData — the exact pattern Cato calls out for Poisson's sandbox-evasion stager that decrypted the PowerShell loader. Tier alerting given the script-from-staging-folder combo is rarely legitimate. Rationale: Cato's hunt list: 'wscript.exe running .vbs files out of user staging folders.' The article also notes the stager had a 'sandbox-evasion delay' before decrypting the PowerShell loader — narrowing path-prefix to Downloads/Temp/AppData covers Poisson's drop spots without firing on legitimate GPO logon scripts in System32 or NETLOGON.
ATT&CKT1059.005 T1204.002 T1497.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Vendor installer that drops a one-off .vbs cleanup script to %TEMP%
  • Adobe/Citrix uninstaller using a VBScript in ProgramData
  • Legacy ERP/accounting client launching a per-user .vbs from AppData
  • User opening an email-attached invoice (still suspicious — likely a true positive in disguise)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msiexec.exe","setup.exe","installer.exe") and InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("services.exe")
Response runbook
Triage: capture the .vbs file and the parent process — was it Outlook, browser, archive utility (WinRAR/7z), or a service? Decode the VBScript looking for the AES/XOR-decrypted PowerShell second stage Cato describes. Contain: kill wscript.exe tree, quarantine the .vbs file and its source archive, isolate the host. Hunt: pivot on the file SHA256, parent-process tree (was it spawned by a browser/mail client?), and any subsequent PowerShell → .NET in-memory loader spawns on the same host within 1h.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has ".vbs"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\", @"\Users\Public\", @"\ProgramData\", @"\Pictures\", @"\Music\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where AccountType =~ "User"
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\wscript.exe" or NewProcessName endswith @"\cscript.exe"
| where CommandLine has ".vbs"
| where CommandLine has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\", @"\Users\Public\", @"\ProgramData\")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

powercfg disabling standby/hibernate to keep host harvest-ready AIActions on Objectives High
Detects powercfg.exe being used to set standby-timeout, hibernate-timeout, monitor-timeout or disk-timeout to 0 — Poisson's trick to prevent the machine sleeping so the local-file keylogger never pauses and he could hand-fetch the keystroke logs. Rationale: Cato's hunt list ends with 'powercfg standby-timeout changes that keep machines awake' — this is the literal article string. Combining standby-timeout/hibernate-timeout/-h off with a zero/off value is the operator-specific shape; powercfg called any other way (e.g. /list, /query) doesn't trip.
ATT&CKT1056.001 T1112 T1562.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IT helpdesk script that disables sleep on conference-room/kiosk machines
  • Visual Studio installer toggling sleep during long compiles
  • Backup software (Veeam, Acronis) pinning the host awake during a job window
  • Power management GPO push from SCCM
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("ccmexec.exe","veeam.backup.shell.exe","sccm.exe") and InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("services.exe")
Response runbook
Triage: who is the AccountName — a sysadmin or a regular user? Pull DeviceFileEvents for new files matching keylogger patterns (*.log/*.txt being appended-to-only by a Python or rundll32 process) and DeviceProcessEvents for python.exe / pythonw.exe spawning from non-standard paths. Contain: revert powercfg ('powercfg -change standby-timeout-ac 20'), isolate the host pending IR. Hunt: across the org for the same powercfg → keylogger file-write pair within 24h and for python.exe processes with PIDs that persist across logon/logoff.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName =~ "powercfg.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("standby-timeout","hibernate-timeout","monitor-timeout","disk-timeout","-change","/change","-setacvalueindex","-setdcvalueindex","-h off","/h off")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(\s|-)0(\b|$)" or ProcessCommandLine has " off"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where AccountType =~ "User"
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\powercfg.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any ("standby-timeout","hibernate-timeout","monitor-timeout","disk-timeout","-change","/change","-h off")
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\s0(\b|$)" or CommandLine has " off"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: powercfg Disables Standby/Hibernate to Keep Host Awake

description: powercfg.exe invoked with standby-timeout / hibernate-timeout / monitor-timeout / disk-timeout set to 0 (or -h off) — Poisson's anti-sleep technique to keep the local-file keylogger harvesting continuously.
references:

      - 'standby-timeout'

      - '/h off'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:(windows.security OR windows.sysmon) @Image:(*\powercfg.exe OR *\POWERCFG.EXE OR *\PowerCfg.exe) @CommandLine:(*standby-timeout* OR *hibernate-timeout* OR *monitor-timeout* OR *disk-timeout* OR *"-h off"* OR *"/h off"*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\powercfg\.exe$/i CommandLine=/(standby-timeout|hibernate-timeout|monitor-timeout|disk-timeout|-h\s+off|\/h\s+off)/i | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name=powercfg.exe AND (Processes.process="*standby-timeout*" OR Processes.process="*hibernate-timeout*" OR Processes.process="*monitor-timeout*" OR Processes.process="*disk-timeout*" OR Processes.process="*-change*" OR Processes.process="*-setacvalueindex*" OR Processes.process="*-setdcvalueindex*" OR Processes.process="*-h off*") AND Processes.process="* 0*" by host Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where user!="*$" | sort - firstTime

Logon-trigger scheduled task at HIGHEST privileges launching script interpreter AIInstallation High
Detects schtasks /Create or PowerShell Register-ScheduledTask creating a task with /SC ONLOGON and /RL HIGHEST that runs a script interpreter (powershell/pwsh/wscript/cscript/mshta/rundll32/regsvr32) — Poisson's pinning technique for at-every-logon highest-privilege persistence. Rationale: Cato's hunt list directly: 'scheduled tasks set to the highest privileges that launch script interpreters.' Three required tokens (Create + HIGHEST + ONLOGON) plus an interpreter payload are vanishingly rare in legitimate management tooling — GPO-deployed tasks typically use SYSTEM, not /RL HIGHEST from a user context.
ATT&CKT1053.005 T1547 T1078.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • RMM agent (NinjaOne/Datto) registering a logon healthcheck task
  • Citrix/VMware EUC client provisioning script
  • Custom IT logon banner script deployed by a sysadmin
  • Java auto-update logon trigger
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("ccmexec.exe","agent.exe","ninjarmm.exe","datto.exe") and InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("services.exe","TrustedInstaller.exe")
Response runbook
Triage: dump the created task XML (`schtasks /Query /TN <name> /XML`), capture the script payload, decode any base64 / -EncodedCommand inside. Contain: delete the task (`schtasks /Delete /TN <name> /F`), revoke and re-test the user account, quarantine any payload files referenced. Hunt: pull all Security 4698 events on the host for the last 60d, cross-reference with DeviceFileEvents for the task's Action path, and search the org for tasks with the same name, author, or payload SHA256.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName =~ "schtasks.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/Create","/CREATE","-Create")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/RL HIGHEST","/RL Highest","-RunLevel Highest")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/SC ONLOGON","/SC OnLogon","ONLOGON","-Trigger")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("powershell","pwsh","wscript","cscript","mshta","rundll32","regsvr32",".vbs",".js",".ps1","cmd.exe /c","cmd /c")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where AccountType =~ "User"
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\schtasks.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any ("/Create","-Create")
| where CommandLine has "HIGHEST"
| where CommandLine has "ONLOGON"
| where CommandLine has_any ("powershell","pwsh","wscript","cscript","mshta","rundll32","regsvr32",".vbs",".ps1")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name=schtasks.exe AND Processes.process="*/Create*" AND Processes.process="*/RL*HIGHEST*" AND Processes.process="*/SC*ONLOGON*" AND (Processes.process="*powershell*" OR Processes.process="*pwsh*" OR Processes.process="*wscript*" OR Processes.process="*cscript*" OR Processes.process="*mshta*" OR Processes.process="*rundll32*" OR Processes.process="*regsvr32*" OR Processes.process="*.vbs*" OR Processes.process="*.ps1*" OR Processes.process="*.js*") by host Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where user!="*$" | sort - firstTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name=schtasks.exe AND Processes.process="*/Create*" AND Processes.process="*/RL*HIGHEST*" AND Processes.process="*/SC*ONLOGON*" AND (Processes.process="*powershell*" OR Processes.process="*pwsh*" OR Processes.process="*wscript*" OR Processes.process="*cscript*" OR Processes.process="*mshta*" OR Processes.process="*rundll32*" OR Processes.process="*regsvr32*" OR Processes.process="*.vbs*" OR Processes.process="*.ps1*" OR Processes.process="*.js*") by host Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where user!="*$" | sort - firstTime
authorized_keys file write on Windows host (SSH key persistence) AIInstallation High
Detects creation or modification of `authorized_keys` under any user `.ssh\` directory or under `%ProgramData%\ssh\` — the file Poisson populated to make his key-based SSH reentry persistent. Tier alerting because authorized_keys writes on a Windows endpoint are nearly always operator-grade. Rationale: The article describes Poisson setting up 'key-based SSH' as the reentry path that survived the C2 takedown — the persistence anchor is the authorized_keys file. On Windows the canonical paths are `%USERPROFILE%\.ssh\authorized_keys` and `%ProgramData%\ssh\administrators_authorized_keys`; either being written by anything other than the user's interactive ssh-keygen flow is suspicious.
ATT&CKT1098.004 T1021.004 T1078.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer setting up SSH access to a GitHub repo and writing their own pubkey
  • IT staff bootstrapping an Ansible/SaltStack control node
  • Visual Studio Code Remote-SSH key copy during initial setup
  • User running ssh-copy-id from WSL
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("ssh-keygen.exe","notepad.exe","code.exe","explorer.exe") or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","pwsh.exe")
Response runbook
Triage: read the authorized_keys file contents — capture every pubkey present and the comments/notes. Pull DeviceLogonEvents for successful SSH inbound logons referencing those keys in the last 30d. Contain: delete the offending lines (or the file), restart sshd, rotate the local user password, force expire any current SSH sessions. Hunt: across the org for authorized_keys writes whose ActingProcess is not ssh-keygen/notepad/code; correlate with Tailscale and OpenSSH-install events on the same host within 7d.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FileName =~ "authorized_keys"
   or FolderPath endswith @"\.ssh\authorized_keys"
   or FolderPath has @"\ProgramData\ssh\"
   or FolderPath has @"\Windows\System32\config\systemprofile\.ssh\"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessAccountDomain
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFileName =~ "authorized_keys"
   or TargetFilePath endswith @"\.ssh\authorized_keys"
   or TargetFilePath has @"\ProgramData\ssh\"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, EventType, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: SSH authorized_keys File Written on Windows Host
id: 0df8cf12-9faf-4f80-faec-8fc1edfdf70a
description: Creation/modification of an OpenSSH authorized_keys file on a Windows endpoint — the persistence step Poisson used to lock in key-based SSH reentry.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/junior-hacker-used-tailscale-and.html
author: thn-usecases
date: 2026/06/17
tags:
  - attack.t1098.004
  - attack.t1021.004
  - attack.t1078.003
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_name:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '\authorized_keys'
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\.ssh\'
      - '\ProgramData\ssh\'
  condition: selection_name or selection_path
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) @EventID:(11 OR 4663) @TargetFilename:(*\\authorized_keys OR *\\.ssh\\* OR *\\ProgramData\\ssh\\* OR *\\.SSH\\*)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten (TargetFileName=/\\authorized_keys$/i OR TargetFileName=/\\\.ssh\\/i OR TargetFileName=/\\ProgramData\\ssh\\/i) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="authorized_keys" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.ssh\\authorized_keys*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\ProgramData\\ssh\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Windows\\System32\\config\\systemprofile\\.ssh\\*") AND Filesystem.action IN ("created","modified","renamed") by host Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | sort - firstTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="authorized_keys" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.ssh\\authorized_keys*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\ProgramData\\ssh\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Windows\\System32\\config\\systemprofile\\.ssh\\*") AND Filesystem.action IN ("created","modified","renamed") by host Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | sort - firstTime
certutil smart-card / certificate store enumeration AIReconnaissance Medium
Detects certutil.exe (or PowerShell Cert: drive enumeration) being used to enumerate Personal/Smart-card cert stores or query CSP/smartcard info — Poisson's late-stage move that Cato reads as recon for certificate-based logins. Rationale: Article: 'probed smart-card and certificate stores (a sign he was eyeing certificate-based logins).' certutil -store/-scinfo/-csplist are the canonical Windows ways to enumerate user/machine cert stores and smart-card CSPs; explicitly excluding the common LOLBin uses (-urlcache, -decode, -hashfile) keeps signal high.
ATT&CKT1555.004 T1552.004 T1087.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IT/PKI admin auditing local cert stores before a smart-card rollout
  • Developer querying Cert:\CurrentUser\My from PowerShell for code-signing
  • Group Policy applying machine-cert auto-enrollment
  • Vendor MSI installer validating its signing cert pre-install
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("ccmexec.exe","sccm.exe","intunemgmt.exe") and AccountName !in~ ("<pki-admin-account>")
Response runbook
Triage: confirm who/what spawned certutil — interactive cmd/PowerShell vs. a service. Pull the same host's DeviceProcessEvents for nearby Havoc/Demon staging behavior (PowerShell with -nop, .NET in-memory loader, shellcode injection into explorer.exe). Contain: if interactive and non-IT, isolate and force interactive logon revalidation; if the user has smart-card auth issued, rotate it. Hunt: across the org, look for the same user account hitting Cert:/certutil -store on multiple hosts within 24h and for any subsequent klist/kerberos ticket use that doesn't match a normal logon flow.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where (FileName =~ "certutil.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-store","-scinfo","-SCInfo","-csplist","-csptest","-key","-user My","-user Root"))
   or (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Cert:\\CurrentUser\\My","Cert:\\LocalMachine\\My","Get-ChildItem Cert:","ls Cert:","dir Cert:"))
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "-urlcache" and ProcessCommandLine !has "-decode" and ProcessCommandLine !has "-encode" and ProcessCommandLine !has "-hashfile"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where AccountType =~ "User"
| where (NewProcessName endswith @"\certutil.exe" and CommandLine has_any ("-store","-scinfo","-csplist","-csptest","-key","-user My"))
   or ((NewProcessName endswith @"\powershell.exe" or NewProcessName endswith @"\pwsh.exe") and CommandLine has "Cert:\\")
| where CommandLine !has "-urlcache" and CommandLine !has "-decode" and CommandLine !has "-hashfile"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: certutil or PowerShell Certificate Store Enumeration
id: 1ef9da23-afa0-4f91-fbfd-9fd2fdfaf81b
description: certutil -store/-scinfo/-csplist or PowerShell Cert:\\ drive enumeration — recon for certificate-based / smart-card logins, the final-week move in the Cato CTRL writeup on 'Poisson'.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/junior-hacker-used-tailscale-and.html
author: thn-usecases
date: 2026/06/17
tags:
  - attack.t1555.004
  - attack.t1552.004
  - attack.t1087.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_certutil:
    Image|endswith: '\certutil.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '-store'
      - '-scinfo'
      - '-csplist'
      - '-csptest'
      - '-key'
  selection_ps:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'Cert:\CurrentUser\My'
      - 'Cert:\LocalMachine\My'
      - 'Get-ChildItem Cert:'
  filter:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '-urlcache'
      - '-decode'
      - '-encode'
      - '-hashfile'
      - '-verify'
  condition: (1 of selection_*) and not filter
level: medium
source:(windows.security OR windows.sysmon) ((@Image:(*\certutil.exe OR *\CertUtil.exe OR *\CERTUTIL.EXE) AND @CommandLine:(*-store* OR *-scinfo* OR *-SCInfo* OR *-csplist* OR *-csptest*) AND NOT @CommandLine:(*-urlcache* OR *-decode* OR *-encode* OR *-hashfile*)) OR (@Image:(*\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe) AND @CommandLine:(*"Cert:\\CurrentUser\\My"* OR *"Cert:\\LocalMachine\\My"*)))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ((ImageFileName=/\\certutil\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/(-store|-scinfo|-csplist|-csptest|-key|-user\s+My)/i AND NOT CommandLine=/(-urlcache|-decode|-encode|-hashfile|-verify)/i) OR (ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/Cert:\\\\(CurrentUser|LocalMachine)\\\\My/i)) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name=certutil.exe AND (Processes.process="*-store*" OR Processes.process="*-scinfo*" OR Processes.process="*-csplist*" OR Processes.process="*-csptest*" OR Processes.process="*-key*" OR Processes.process="*-user*My*")) OR ((Processes.process_name=powershell.exe OR Processes.process_name=pwsh.exe) AND (Processes.process="*Get-ChildItem*Cert:*" OR Processes.process="*ls*Cert:\\CurrentUser\\My*" OR Processes.process="*Cert:\\CurrentUser\\My*")) by host Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where user!="*$" | where NOT match(process, "(?i)-urlcache|-decode|-encode|-hashfile|-verify") | sort - firstTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name=certutil.exe AND (Processes.process="*-store*" OR Processes.process="*-scinfo*" OR Processes.process="*-csplist*" OR Processes.process="*-csptest*" OR Processes.process="*-key*" OR Processes.process="*-user*My*")) OR ((Processes.process_name=powershell.exe OR Processes.process_name=pwsh.exe) AND (Processes.process="*Get-ChildItem*Cert:*" OR Processes.process="*ls*Cert:\\CurrentUser\\My*" OR Processes.process="*Cert:\\CurrentUser\\My*")) by host Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where user!="*$" | where NOT match(process, "(?i)-urlcache|-decode|-encode|-hashfile|-verify") | sort - firstTime
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("100.100.100.2") or RemoteUrl has_any ("duckdns.org", "login.tailscale.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["100.100.100.2"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["duckdns.org", "login.tailscale.com"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:
        DestinationHostname:
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    condition: selection_ip or selection_domain
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive IOC match
level: critical
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("100.100.100.2")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("duckdns.org", "login.tailscale.com")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("duckdns.org", "login.tailscale.com")

     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("100.100.100.2")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("duckdns.org", "login.tailscale.com")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("duckdns.org", "login.tailscale.com")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02

    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'

FortiBleed leak exposes Fortinet VPN credentials for 73,000 devices.

BleepingComputer
2026-06-17 6 use cases 1 technique 5 kill-chain phases detected

A newly discovered data leak dubbed "FortiBleed" has exposed what appears to be a collection of Fortinet and FortiGate VPN credentials for 73,932 firewall URLs at organizations worldwide. [...]
